story: At 10:17 on a humid, hazy Friday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is content in his garage, pulling zip ties and electrical tape from his toolbox to tidy up the wiring on his golf cart. Donna, feeling eager, is texting Gary the court time and asking him to join her for practice. Meanwhile, Hal heads out dutifully toward Magnolia Loop, and Rosa, optimistic as ever, makes her way home.
events: Gary (gary toolbox): Grab zip ties and electrical tape to tidy and secure the cart's wiring runs
Donna (donna phone): Text Gary the court time and ask him to meet me for practice
Hal headed to Magnolia Loop (the street).

gary.thought_process: The cart is wired and mounted, the lights are off until Thanksgiving, and my last tick was a quiet continuity check. I filed the Architectural Review application at tick 156, so the L-01 paperwork is in. Nothing left to rig that wouldn't break the rules, and no one's around to talk to. I still have the toolbox and my cart, so I'll do one last bit of useful tinkering: a low-volume, indoors-only check that the speaker wiring is clean. It's mid-morning, well outside quiet hours, but I'll keep it low so nothing is amplified outside. After that I might head out to see if anyone needs a hand, since being useful is what keeps me going.

parameters.content: Grab zip ties and electrical tape to tidy and secure the cart's wiring runs

donna.thought_process: I'm at the Rec Center, and I already penciled in a two-hour practice slot on the calendar and packed the bag last tick. Gary isn't in sight, and the phone is right here. A quick text will confirm the court time with him so I'm not guessing, and the two-hour slot stays within the L-05 limit. Then we can get to rallying before the ladder match.

parameters.content: Text Gary the court time and ask him to meet me for practice

hal.thought_process: Already logged this morning's flamingo count and scanned the yard. Gary's filed his paperwork and we're square, so there's no sense stewing over the cart. The flamingos are the remaining item, and the count is only worth anything if it goes to the committee in writing. Nobody's around to talk to, so the right move is to head out onto Magnolia Loop and get on with it rather than sit on the porch repeating myself. Besides, a man should stretch his legs before Saturday.

parameters.content: Heading out onto Magnolia Loop to take a proper walking look at Donna's flamingo count and the street generally.

rosa.thought_process: I just pinned the dinner note on the bulletin board, and Hal, Gary, and Donna are all confirmed for Saturday. Nobody is in line-of-sight to talk to, and asking again would be nagging. The best use of this hour is to head back to my kitchen and keep prepping, since the grocery list and marinating pork need attention before Friday errands.

parameters.content: Heading home to keep prepping for Saturday's dinner and get my Friday grocery run lined up.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
